title: Knowledge check: Survival Analysis

questions.prompt: For “Survival Analysis”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Specialist methods carry domain-specific data requirements and assumptions; choosing a package does not replace subject-matter validation. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Survival Analysis” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Time-to-Event Data” as part of lesson 233. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Survival Analysis” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Name the domain assumptions, inspect the input schema and define a diagnostic or sensitivity check before interpretation. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
